messages:
asha: quick heads-up — I ran a quantized-sweep on the kernel-chooser branch and hit an odd perf regression on longer contexts (4k+). wanted to dump notes here and see if anyone has obvious blind spots.

dev-bot: automated run summary attached (run id run-2026-03-06-0912). main variants: fp16-baseline, fp8-true, int8-ema-calib. warmup=250 tokens, steady=3m, powercap=210W.

samir: can you paste the exact runner args? kernel selection + quant flags often change default batching heuristics.

asha: sure — command:``` 
./runner --model llama-65b --seq 4096 --warmup 250 --steady 180 --power-limit 210 \ 
  --quant-mode=fp8 --kernel-chooser=dynamic-v2 --calib=ema:steps=500
```

olga: two quick checks: (1) when you use dynamic kernel chooser, do you get mixed kernels (fp8 for matmuls, fp16 for softmax)? (2) kv cache allocation strategy — are we compacting KV between batches? those blow up long-context numbers.

asha: we do see a mix. logs show: "chosen_kernels: matmul_fp8, softmax_fp16, kv_copy_fp16". kv pages look fragmented; peak GPU mem is ~39.2G vs baseline 36.7G.

ben: fragmentation + extra memcpy is a perf killer for p95 on long contexts. calibration can change activation ranges and make more ops fallback to slower paths too. what were latency numbers?

asha: short dump from the trace:``` 
baseline fp16: p50=22ms p95=88ms tokens/s=1430
fp8 (current): p50=18ms p95=142ms tokens/s=1210
int8-ema: p50=20ms p95=110ms tokens/s=1285
```
so fp8 improved p50 but p95 regressed badly. throughput down vs baseline.

samir: that pattern screams tail amplification from KV eviction/compaction bursts. p50 benefits from faster matmuls but p95 spikes when GC/compact happens. we should instrument time spent in kv_copy / alloc / free.

olga: agree. add a micro-trace with these hooks:``` 
trace.add_point("kv_alloc_start")
trace.add_point("kv_compact_start")
trace.add_point("kernel_launch_matmul")
```
and run a short 30s workload with synthetic prefix sizes to force compaction.

asha: will do. one more note: int8 run used per-layer calibration with activation hist bins=2048; fp8 used global ema scale. do we expect per-layer to reduce mem churn?

ben: per-layer calib tends to produce tighter ranges -> fewer overflows but can increase num ops selecting "narrow" kernels which sometimes are slower (more branches). try fp8 with per-layer calib and fp16 fallback threshold tuned. also compare warmup lengths. our earlier bench showed p95 stabilizes only after ~400 warmup tokens on FP8 for long seq.

asha: interesting — I used 250 warmup because that's what we normally do for 2k. i'll rerun with 500 warmup and add per-layer fp8 calib. also will flip kernel-chooser to static mapping to see if dynamic choice is causing thrash.

dev-bot: queued run(s): run-1936543210-a (fp8/per-layer/warmup500/static), run-1936543210-b (fp8/ema/warmup500/static), run-1936543210-c (fp8/per-layer/warmup500/dynamic). expected finish ~1936545400.

samir: for fair comparisons please: (1) cap TDP the same across runs (you did 210W) (2) same tokenizer seed/order (subtokenization changes token counts) (3) run each variant >=3 reps and report mean + stdev for p50/p95/tokens-s.

asha: noted. also will attach exact seed and prompt set (1000 eval prompts we use for perf-suites).

olga: small gotcha — calibration step counts matter. per-layer with 500 steps gave us different inference-time branching in earlier tests versus 2k steps. log the calib artifact hash so we can reproduce.

asha: yup will upload calib artifacts to s3://redwood-quant/artifacts/run-1936543210/ and paste URLs here when done.

ben: once we have traces, i'll run our profiler diff tool to attribute p95 to kernel vs memcpy vs allocator. quick tip: when reporting tokens/s, normalize by decoded tokens (post-tokenizer) not raw characters.

asha: thanks all. i'm going to run the three variants now with added KV traces and 500 warmup. will report back with artifacts + perf table. :thumbsup:
